candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide education and interventions that promote health, reduce risk, and support age-appropriate wellness and prevention
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — older-adult fall prevention / exercise
candidate.educational_objective: Teach older adults at risk for falls to include exercises that improve leg strength and balance as part of fall prevention.

options.A: Include exercises that strengthen the legs and improve balance
options.B: Avoid physical activity to reduce the chance of falling
options.C: Use flexibility exercise alone and omit balance work
options.D: Use only upper-body strengthening because leg strength does not affect fall risk

candidate.rationale: Current CDC guidance for preventing older-adult falls specifically recommends strength and balance exercises and gives Tai Chi as an example. CDC STEADI resources also assess leg strength, balance, and mobility as fall-risk factors. Therefore A is the best answer. Avoiding activity or omitting balance/leg-strength work conflicts with current fall-prevention guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC recommends exercises that strengthen the legs and improve balance to help prevent falls in older adults.
candidate.source_document_title: Preventing Falls and Hip Fractures — Older Adult Fall Prevention
candidate.source_locator: Preventing a fall or hip fracture → DO STRENGTH AND BALANCE EXERCISES: do exercises that make the legs stronger and improve balance; Tai Chi is provided as an example
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: Which exercise advice is consistent with current CDC fall-prevention guidance for an older adult?
